request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient: Maghrebian 8.2 year-old boy
Admission Date: [Date]
Discharge Date: [Date]
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course Summary:

The patient was admitted for evaluation due to moderate mental retardation, mild intellectual disability, hyperactive behavior, and partial secondary generalized epilepsy with persistent atypical absences and psychogenic episodes. The physical and neurological exam revealed no abnormal findings. The EEG showed abnormal discharges of slow waves and spikes and bi-temporally localized waves. The MRI study showed cortico-subcortical atrophy and corpus callosum hypoplasia. A high definition karyotype and metabolic panel results were normal.

Valproic acid was administered to manage the seizures and hyperkinetic behavior. The patient's condition improved, leading to his discharge.

The genetic study showed 116 bases deletion in genomic sequence of EN2 gene: 155462376–155462491 (G1 marker). The patient showed abnormalities in the transcription of the EN2 gene, that implies the deletion of 208 bases (between 1493 and 1719 bases of the complementary sequence, C4 marker).

The patient has been discharged with improved symptoms and has been advised to continue the medications prescribed by the treating physician. A follow-up visit has been scheduled to assess the patient's progress with regard to the aforementioned symptoms.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
The episode centres on epilepsy: partial secondary generalized epilepsy with persistent atypical absences. It was investigated with EEG and MRI and treated with valproic acid. The intellectual disability, hyperactivity and genetic findings are background conditions, and the treatment was aimed at the seizures.

In ICD-10-AM, epilepsy falls in G40 (epilepsy). Localization-related (focal) epilepsy is G40.0–G40.2, and generalized epilepsy is G40.3–G40.4. Atypical absences fall under G40.3, and "partial secondary generalized" suggests focal seizures evolving to generalized ones, which is G40.2 or G40.1. Either way the three-character category is G40.

The alternative is F71 or F70 for the intellectual disability, as the admission was "for evaluation due to" several problems. The treatment and investigations (EEG, valproate) were directed at the epilepsy, so I chose G40.

CODE: G40
